newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Row delays Australia euthanasia debate.
newsitem.headline: Row delays Australia euthanasia debate.

text.p: The Australian parliament was forced to postpone its debate on Thursday on a move to quash the world's first voluntary euthanasia law after an opposition politician was thrown out of parliament for disorderly conduct.

The House of Representatives' main committee had been scheduled to resume debate on a backbencher's motion that would see Canberra use its constitutional powers to overturn the law, introduced in Australia's remote Northern Territory.

But the meeting was suspended before debate resumed when opposition politician Mark Latham became embroiled in an argument with deputy speaker Garry Nehl over whether the debate should be moved to parliament's main chamber.

Nehl ended the committee meeting and referred the matter to the main chamber, which suspended Latham from parliament for 24 hours for disorderly conduct in refusing to leave the committee's meeting when told to by Nehl.
A parliamentary official told Reuters debate would resume next week.
The Northern Territory's euthanasia law, passed last year, came into operation in July. The first person to use the law, cancer patient Bob Dent, died in September.
